narrative.northStar: Güvenilir Rehberlik Masası (The Trusted Guidance Desk) — with a landing-scoped sub-world: Yerleştirme Kılavuzu (The Placement Guide)
narrative.overview: Hedefim Lise sits with an anxious 8th-grader (and their parent, and their counselor) at the moment a life choice is being made, and its whole job is to feel like a calm, credible desk to make that choice at. The system runs on a deliberate duality: a deep-navy chrome world — the sticky navbar (#0a0f1c), the footer, and the dark page headers on interior surfaces — frames the product like a confident night sky you're navigating by, while the body is a bright, orderly workspace of near-white canvas, cool slate neutrals, and a single decisive blue. Scope note (2026-08): the landing route (/) no longer uses the old dark-navy #071426 hero with aurora glows; it runs its own light, landing-scoped document world — 'Yerleştirme Kılavuzu' — on a cool paper ground (#f3f5f4) with petrol teal (#0c4a45) as authority/action and vermilion (#dc5a34) as the single warm signal for the user's own position, set in Archivo + Source Serif 4 + mono micro-labels. Everything else stays Exam Blue.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, trustworthy chrome (navbar, footer, interior page headers) over a bright, scannable data body.
One decisive accent (Exam Blue) rationed against a broad cool-slate neutral field.
Soft, resting surfaces — generous radii, hairline borders, whisper-light shadows.
Semantic color (emerald/rose/amber) used only to carry meaning, never decoration.
Calm density: roomy on marketing surfaces, efficient but never cramped in tools.
Landing-scoped document world (.landing only): paper ground, teal authority, one vermilion 'sen' signal, poster-scale tabular figures, mono micro-label meta-grammar.

rules.name: The One-Signal Rule
rules.body: Exam Blue is the only color that invites action. It should cover well under ~10% of any body screen — its scarcity is what makes 'act here' legible. Never use blue as a decorative fill.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Emerald, rose, and amber never appear for decoration — each is a claim (good / destructive / caution). If a color isn't carrying meaning, it's slate.

rules.name: The Two-Worlds Rule (amended 2026-08)
rules.body: Cyan and glow treatments live only in the dark chrome world (navbar, footer, dark interior page headers). The light Exam Blue body is blue-and-slate. The old third member — the dark aurora hero — no longer exists: the landing is now its own light document world, and neither cyan, aurora glows, nor Exam Blue may appear inside it.

rules.name: The Heavy-Head Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight, not size alone: headings are 700–800 with slightly negative tracking; body stays 400–500. Never set a heading below 700.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Label Rule
rules.body: Category/meta text is uppercase, bold, wide-tracked, and tiny (≤11px). It is a texture, not a headline — never uppercase running copy.

rules.name: The Flat-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and defined by their hairline border. Shadow is a response to state (hover, focus) — never ambient decoration on a static card.

rules.name: The Sen Rule (landing)
rules.body: Vermilion marks exactly one thing: you. It never fills a button, tints a card, or decorates. If vermilion appears, it is either the user's position on the scale or an error the user must act on.

rules.name: The One-Authority Rule (landing)
rules.body: Teal is the only action color on the landing. Exam Blue never crosses into .landing; teal/vermilion never leave it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule (landing)
rules.body: Every numeral that represents data gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (the .tabular utility).

rules.name: The Turkish-Comma Rule (landing)
rules.body: Every percentile prints with a comma decimal (5,00, %1,23) via the shared fmt() pattern. Never a dot.

rules.name: The Sort-Not-Filter Rule (landing)
rules.body: The percentile input is a sort signal, never a threshold filter: submit routes to /okullar sorted by percentile. No school is ever hidden by the user's number.

dos: Do ration Exam Blue (#2563eb) to the single most important action per surface; keep it well under ~10% of a body screen.
Do define surfaces with hairline Line (#e2e8f0) borders and keep them flat at rest; let shadow appear only on hover/focus.
Do use the uppercase, bold, wide-tracked ≤11px label for category/meta text, and carry hierarchy with weight (700–800 heads).
Do keep radii in the 12 / 16–24px family and never mix radii within one component.
Do reserve emerald/rose/amber for genuine meaning (success / destructive / caution).
Do confine cyan and glow treatments to the dark chrome world (navbar, footer, dark interior page headers) only.
Do carry all landing meta text in the mono micro-label voice (10–11px, uppercase, 0.14–0.18em tracking, ink-faint).
Do keep landing panels flat: Line hairline + shadow-sm, hover states only.
donts: Don't mix gray-* and slate-* neutrals; the system is slate — legacy gray-* classes (mobile sheets) are drift to migrate.
Don't introduce a second accent hue into the Exam Blue body; blue is the only action color there.
Don't put gradient-clipped text or cyan glows on body/data surfaces — they belong to the dark chrome world, and the old hero devices (aurora, gradient keyword) are retired entirely.
Don't cross the landing boundary in either direction: no Exam Blue/cyan inside .landing, no landing teal/vermilion/Archivo/Source Serif on Exam Blue surfaces.
Don't add ambient drop-shadows to resting cards; depth is tonal + hairline first.
Don't set headings below 700 weight or uppercase running body copy.
Don't use vermilion for anything but the user's position or an actionable error on the landing.
Don't turn the landing percentile input into a filter, print a percentile with a dot decimal, or set data numerals without .tabular.
